chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about water from which a chicken had drunk, so he said:
If there is filth on its beak, wudu (ablution) is not to be performed with it, and do not drink. But if no filth is known to be on its beak, then perform wudu (ablution) with it and drink.

key_terms.تَوَضَّأْ: perform wudu (ablution) with it when no impurity is known
key_terms.دَجَاجَةٌ: a chicken whose contact with the water is being evaluated
key_terms.قَذَرٌ: dirt or filth affecting the ruling of purity
key_terms.مَاءٍ: water under discussion for purity and use
key_terms.مِنْقَارِهَا: its beak, the point of contact relevant to possible contamination
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأْ: to perform wudu (ablution) with the water

ai.seo_question: Can water be used for wudu (ablution) or drinking after a chicken has drunk from it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about water touched by a chicken’s beak. If impurity is known to be present on the beak, the water should not be used for wudu (ablution) or drinking; if no impurity is known, the water remains usable.
